subject: Tracefield onboarding & qualification for NebulaCorp integration
messages:

Subject: Tracefield onboarding & qualification for NebulaCorp integration

Hi Claire / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the Telemetry/Observability scope for the LLM integration. High-level notes from discovery: 

- Goal: instrument inferences served via Redwood so NebulaCorp can correlate user requests to your request logs and APM traces (must include trace IDs, latency breakdowns, and per-model token metrics).
- Constraints: SOC2/PCI environment; logs forwarded to your Splunk instance; 3rd-party PII redaction on payloads.
- Primary integration surface: Redwood SDK + HTTP headers from your gateway for trace correlation; optional prefix/KV cache metrics for latency optimization.

As next steps I suggest: 
1) Confirm the exact trace header names you prefer (we can default to x-rdwd-trace-id / traceparent).
2) Monica (SE) to propose a minimal telemetry handshake (header names, sample structured log fields, latency breakdown header) and an SDK snippet for your engineering team.
3) Align on attachments/evidence you need for procurement (SOC2 artifacts, data retention policy).

I'm looping in Monica and Jordan to draft the telemetry handshake and a short SDK sample. Monica — can you put together a 1-pager + example curl and list any server-side config we need to enable on the Redwood side?

Claire — if you can confirm preferred trace header names and whether you need signed audit logs (HMAC) for each call that helps prioritize.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — helpful recap. A couple of clarifications from our infra team: 

- Trace headers: we prefer propagation via W3C traceparent if possible. If Redwood exposes a lightweight duplicate header for quick lookups, we like x-nebula-trace-id to map in our dashboards.
- Latency breakdown: we need at minimum three buckets surfaced per request in headers or logs: queuing_ms, decode_ms, downstream_ms. A single header like x-rdwd-latency-breakdown: queuing=12;decode=84;downstream=3 would be fine.
- Security: SOC2 evidence is required. We need to validate that trace payloads do not contain PII; can Redwood provide redaction guidance and a short checklist for engineers?

Also: we will run your SDK behind our API gateway. How does the Redwood SDK pick up incoming trace context from upstream headers (e.g., traceparent -> internal propagation)? Will the SDK include automatic log enrichment or do we have to add fields manually to our app logs?

Let's plan a technical 30-min sync with your SEs next week.

—Claire

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@nebulacorp.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tracefield onboarding & qualification for NebulaCorp integration

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear asks. Summary below along with concrete examples you can hand to your eng team. I kept it minimal for an initial handshake; we can expand after the technical sync.

1) Header propagation and naming
- We fully support W3C traceparent. Redwood SDK will, by default, read traceparent from incoming requests and propagate it internally to model inference spans.
- Optional duplicate header for quick dashboard joins: x-nebula-trace-id (string UUID). If present, we pass it along as an attribute on the inference span.
- Recommended header names: traceparent (W3C), x-nebula-trace-id (optional), x-rdwd-trace-id (Redwood internal).

2) Latency breakdown
- We can surface a single response header: x-rdwd-latency-breakdown: queuing=12;decode=84;downstream=3
- We also emit equivalent structured fields in the inference span: rdwd.queuing_ms, rdwd.decode_ms, rdwd.downstream_ms. These are available in traces and our export to OTLP if you ingest via your APM.

3) Structured log / trace fields (minimal set)
- rdwd.trace_id (string)
- rdwd.span_id (string)
- rdwd.model (string)
- rdwd.user_hash (string, sha256)
- rdwd.request_tokens (int)
- rdwd.response_tokens (int)
- rdwd.queuing_ms (int)
- rdwd.decode_ms (int)

4) SDK behavior (what we do automatically)
- Automatic extraction: reads traceparent and x-nebula-trace-id from upstream headers.
- Auto-enrichment: when the SDK emits logs/traces it adds rdwd.* fields and a correlation id in logs.
- Redaction: SDK offers a redact_payloads option (default off). With redact_payloads=true we strip likely PII fields from JSON bodies and replace with [REDACTED]. We'll include recommended regexes and a short checklist for SOC2 review.

5) Embeddings & re-ranker correlation
- Embedding requests can accept rdwd.parent_trace_id in the request body/metadata. We recommend reusing the same trace_id for all downstream calls spawned by a parent inference to enable a single timeline in traces.

6) Examples (snippet)
- curl example:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/inference \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redwood_key>' \
  -H 'traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01' \
  -H 'x-nebula-trace-id: 0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e' \
  -d '{"input":"Summarize...","metadata":{"user_hash":"<sha256>"}}'

- SDK pseudocode (Python):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(redact_payloads=True)
# SDK will extract traceparent from incoming headers and attach rdwd.* fields automatically
resp = client.generate(input, metadata={"user_hash": user_hash})

7) Deliverables for sync
- I will attach an updated redwood-tracefield-spec.md with the header names, sample logs, and the SOC2 redaction checklist.
- Proposed time: Thu Apr 29 10:00–10:30 PT. Jordan — can you confirm?

If you'd like I can also include a short OTLP exporter example showing how to map rdwd.* attributes into your Splunk/OTLP pipeline.

—Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- W3C traceparent + x-nebula-trace-id is perfect. We'll adopt rdwd.* as the attribute namespace in our mapping.
- Latency header format works for our dashboard parser.
- Please include the redaction regexes in the spec before the sync so our compliance team can pre-review.

I'll take Thu Apr 29 10:00 PT. I've created a short Confluence page with our current logging pipeline and SOC items: https://nebulacorp.atlassian.net/l/cp/XYZ-telemetry-handbook — Rajiv and I will add a few examples.
